subject: dragonling
pitch: A baby dragon the size of a house cat, sitting proudly beside the broken shell of its speckled egg. Teal scales fading to a buttery belly, stubby horns, a row of soft orange spines down its back, oversized wings it can't fly with yet, with translucent amber skin between the fingers, and a chubby tail ending in a little spade. Big amber eyes, a toothy grin and a wisp of smoke curling from one nostril.
reasoning:
I'm planning the scene proportions and layout for a TypeScript SDK module depicting a small sitting baby dragon beside a broken egg, sized relative to a house cat, and working out the coordinate system and pose for the sitting figure.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy for the dragon — hips as root joint, spine chain up through chest, neck, head, and a separate jaw joint, plus leg chains branching from the hips. I'm reasoning through how capsule parts attach to bones via weight functions, confirming that passing a joint directly into the capsule builder lets it inherit that joint's skinning weights automatically.

Still designing wing structure...

I'll simplify: membrane edges running from shoulder through wrist to outer fingertip, paired with a trailing body edge, plus finger capsules radiating outward and a row of spikes along the back computed from positions along the spine.

For coloring, I'll apply teal countershading (dark back, lighter belly) along with a scale-texture paint layered over the body meshes. For the tail, I'll build it as a chain/sweep along a polyline path so it tapers naturally along its length.

Working out the axis orientation so the spade sits flat horizontally at the tail tip, computing the cross product of the chosen x and y vectors to get the correct normal direction.

Now I'm defining the spade outline points as coordinates extending backward from the tail origin, placing the spade tip farthest back and making sure the ordering goes counterclockwise without self-intersecting.

For the head, I'll attach a sphere geometry to the head joint using the part helper with position offsets, keeping the setup simple. For the eyes, I'm planning amber-colored spheres with small dark scaled spheres as pupils to create a slit-like appearance.

Now I'm working out the smoke wisp as a sweep along a catmull spiral path with tapering radius and a light grey color, anchored near the head's nostril joint since the path has no explicit weights. Then I'm considering a lathe-based egg shape, possibly broken open with speckled texture.

Still defining the egg profile points...

I'll close the lathe shape back to the axis and add speckled paint texture to the eggshell using small irregular spots in muted colors, then position the egg near the dragon.

Now I'm placing the egg at roughly x=-0.13 resting on the ground plane, sized about 0.13 across and 0.11 tall relative to the dragon's larger scale. Next I'm planning the dragon's body itself, considering a lofted sweep through several cross-section stations for the sitting pose facing forward.

Working out the hip and chest stations...

Rescaling slightly smaller: hips at 0.075, chest 0.15, neck 0.21, head 0.25, with head sphere radius 0.05. I'm now setting up the body loft using the hips-chest-neck bone chain, defining stations along that path for the mesh cross-sections.

I'm sketching station positions to get the dragon sitting naturally with the rump resting near ground level and the chest tilting forward-upward, then thinking through how to paint the belly lighter using a countershade based on normal direction — acknowledging that relying on normal.y isn't perfect for a seated pose where the belly faces more forward-down.

Instead I'm switching to a custom paint function blending a teal scale pattern with a mottled golden belly color, using the point's z-position and normal's z-component to determine where the ventral patch shows on the front of the chest rather than the top.

Still writing paint logic...

Writing gradient blend code...

I'll simplify the body paint to just belly versus scales, and plan an orange spine row with spikes positioned in a loop running up the back, interpolating z and y along the spine curve.

Still working out spine coordinates...

Now I'm working out the sitting pose: front legs short with claws, back legs folded with feet forward on the ground. I'm defining hip, knee, and ankle joints with approximate positions, building thigh and shin as capsules connecting them with appropriate radius.

Adding foot geometry as a flattened scaled sphere with toes... and continuing to define arm joints (shoulder, elbow) parented to the chest for the front limbs.

For the sitting pose I'm placing the arms down with hands near the ground, and separately working out the wing rig: a wingShoulder joint off the chest that spreads outward and up, with wingElbow and wing-wrist joints positioned to suggest oversized, not-yet-flight-ready wings held partly open.

Still defining wing joints...

I'll set edgeB to run from a flank point near the chest to finger4L, letting the membrane span between two polylines of different lengths using parametric ratios along each. Since Joint qualifies as a FrameInput and thus a PointInput, these arrays of joints should work fine as PathInput for the membrane edges.

For the membrane itself, I'll use default smooth skinning across joint weights, give it a thin 0.004 thickness, and color it amber (#e8a04a) since opacity isn't supported. To avoid duplicating all the geometry for both wings, I'll write a helper function that takes a sign parameter (1 for left, -1 for right) and mirrors the x-coordinates while appending L/R suffixes to joint names.

Now I'm adding stubby horns on the head using spike primitives anchored near the head sphere, angled outward and slightly back, with a small radius and a cream-orange color to contrast the amber membrane.

Then I'm shaping the muzzle: a sphere scaled slightly for the snout attached to the head bone, plus defining a jaw joint parented to the head to build out the lower jaw as a separate capsule piece.

For the teeth, I'm adding small white cone-shaped spikes along the mouth line—upper ones pointing down from the snout, lower ones pointing up from the jaw—to create a toothy grin effect.

For the eyes, I'm placing amber spheres with darker elongated pupils positioned slightly forward, and checking the geometry so the eye spheres protrude naturally from the head sphere's surface rather than sinking inside it.

Now I'm working out the nostril smoke effect — defining a curling catmull-rom path starting at the nostril position and drifting upward and outward, swept with a gradually widening radius and a soft gray color to look like wisps of smoke. I'm also noting I still need to add the egg and some ground geometry to round out the scene.

Plotting the tail curve with catmull points trailing back and curling upward toward a spade-shaped tip, keeping the spade plane oriented per the earlier geometry calculation.

Deciding to orient the spade facing the viewer in the XY plane, standing upright with its tip pointing up for better readability—then sketching its outline coordinates with the stem meeting the tail.

Still working out spade geometry...

Defining the tail chain...

Scale and paint helpers look fine as-is, and foot placement should sit flush with the ground given the joint heights. Now I'm setting up the imports, pulling in only the builder functions I actually need like createBuilder, paint, scales, mottle, and spots.

Defining scale and belly colors...

Writing the dragon builder...

Setting the jaw's aim direction forward for the hinge, then starting a loop to mirror the hip joints across left and right sides using a sign multiplier for X.

Still defining leg geometry...

Adding claw spikes with offset positions and a pale color, then setting up the shoulder joint for the front legs with aim parameters toward the elbow position.

Continuing the arm chain down to the elbow and paw joints, I'm building capsule segments for the upper and lower arm plus a flattened paw sphere with small claws, then starting a wing root joint off the chest for the wing structure.

Still defining finger joints...

Now I'm figuring out the membrane edges, planning a leading edge from the elbow through the wrist to the digits, then connecting digit tips to form the trailing edge of the wing membrane.

I'm defining edgeB using a body anchor point near the wing root, then thinking through how membrane weights should inherit from the joint chains so the wrist and digits drive deformation naturally, with grid vertices interpolated between the two edges based on arc-length parameterization.

Adding more capsule segments...

Now I'm setting up the body loft, projecting the hips, chest, and neck joints onto the catmull path stations so the sweep radii interpolate correctly between them, with the belly region covered by the paint layer.

For the spine spikes, I'm computing 8 evenly spaced positions along the back, orange-colored, deriving their y-position from an approximate linear interpolation of the body's cross-section height at each z-depth along the spine.

I'm placing soft orange spikes along the ridge with directional offsets and tapering lengths, then setting up the tail as a catmull-rom chain with four joints for smooth articulation.

I'm checking the tail's parent attachment, confirming it should bind near the hips bone segment since that's the closest joint to the tail's starting point. For the tail shape itself I'm sweeping a tapering radius along its length to give it a chubby base that narrows toward the tip.

Now I'm designing a spade shape to extrude at the tail's tip, picking an orange tone for the color and working out an outline of points that form the classic spade silhouette, oriented so its width sits within the tail's visible radius.

For the egg, I'm planning a lathed profile at the body's side using a shell color with a speckled paint pattern—mixing muted browns and greens as spots over a cream base—and setting enough lathe segments for smoothness.

Checking the egg placement at x=-0.15 with radius 0.066, the gap looks fine, and positioning it at [-0.15, 0, 0.02] with the lathe axis along y seems right.

Now I'm placing the eyes and pupils for character S, setting the eye sphere on the head bone at a specific offset, then adding a scaled pupil slightly in front of it to make sure it sits just outside the eye's surface rather than clipping into it.

I'm placing the head sphere using the joint's default position, then adding a snout sphere slightly forward and scaled for shape. Now I'm working out the jaw structure, positioning a lower jaw joint and capsule beneath the snout in skin color to form the mouth area.

I'm figuring out the grin by placing small cone-shaped teeth along the upper and lower jaw lines, calculating their base coordinates and orientation so the upper teeth point downward and lower teeth point upward, with four teeth per side.

Working out the ellipsoid surface height at the snout's teeth position, I settle on teeth base around y=0.21 with the spike directed downward so they protrude below the surface for a toothy grin look. Now I'm placing the nostril for a smoke effect near the front of the snout.

I'm setting up a curved catmull-rom path for smoke rising from the nostril with increasing radius and a light gray-blue color, weighted to the head bone since it starts there. Then I move on to defining the horn spikes — left and right pairs angled outward and backward with tan coloring — before starting on orange spine spikes.

For the shell, I'm extruding a flat triangular shard lying along the ground plane with a thin thickness, positioned so its bottom edge sits right at the floor. I'm also considering a paw element as a scaled sphere at the paw joint, elongated and flattened for a more foot-like shape.

Next I'm laying out the leg joints and limb capsules—hip, thigh, knee, shin, ankle, and foot—checking radii and positions so each segment's lowest point rests just above the ground. I'm also verifying the body loft station at the rump keeps its bottom edge clear of the floor, then double-checking how capsule joints accept point and frame inputs for the leg connections.

Now I'm defining unique joint names across both sides—hips, knees, ankles, shoulders, elbows, paws, and wing segments including root, elbow, wrist, and four digits per wing—using a mirrored loop so left and right sides share logic but flip sign. I'm placing the wing wrist and digit tip coordinates, then working out the direction vectors from wrist to each digit tip to shape the wing's spread.

I'm also sketching out capsule radii for the wing bones and thinking through the membrane edge paths connecting elbow, wrist, and digits—adjusting digit positions so the leading edge doesn't zigzag awkwardly and the membrane folds naturally across the wing.

I'll simplify the trailing edge to go straight from flank to digit1, skipping digit4, and keep digit2/digit4 as internal struts rather than boundary points for the membrane mesh.

The flank point position is slightly outside the body width at the chest, but that seems acceptable for the membrane attachment.

I'm confirming the membrane call needs color and thickness, then setting up the sphere geometry with segment counts derived from b.segments. I'm double-checking that parts without explicit placement default correctly to the joint position, and making sure the spike helper takes a base and direction/tip point along with length and radius parameters.

Now I'm writing a loop generating spine spikes along the body, computing height and taper based on position, checking that each spike's base sits just above the body surface at that z-coordinate.

Then I'm building the tail as a chain following a smooth curve through four control points, starting inside the rump and curving upward and backward, with four joints connecting the segments and radii tapering along the tail's length.

Now I'm reviewing other details: skipping extra tail spikes, hooking up the hip, chest, and neck joints into the body loft, adding speckles and spots to the egg surface with appropriate lathe segments, and confirming all imports (builder, paint, scales, mottle, spots, THREE) are actually used before finalizing the code.

Defining the color palettes and paint functions—teal scales for the body, a mottled belly texture, and a rule that applies the belly pattern only to the lower front snout area while keeping the rest scaled. I'm also setting up wing and eye colors, checking that the paint logic correctly distinguishes head from belly regions based on position.

Now I'm writing the full builder structure, starting with metadata and the joint hierarchy—hips as the root, then chest, neck, head, and jaw, each with position and direction values defining the dragon's pose. I'm making sure joint roles like "neck", "head", and "jaw" are assigned correctly so the rig behaves as expected.

Building the body loft...
